ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the electromotive force of the power supply is $E{=}12\mathrm{V}$. Lamp $A$ is labeled "10V, 10W"; lamp $B$ only has the label 9V, and the maximum resistance of the rheostat is $180\Omega$. When the sliding contact $C$ moves to point $E$, lamp $A$ lights up normally, and when $C$ moves to point $F$, lamp $B$ lights up normally (points $E$ and $F$ are the endpoints of the rheostat).

1. What is the resistance of lamp $A$?
2. What is the internal resistance of the power supply?
3. What is the rated power of lamp $B$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the electromotive force of the power supply is $E=12\mathrm{V}$. Lamp $A$ is labeled "10V, 10W"; lamp $B$ is only labeled 9V, and the maximum resistance of the rheostat is $180\Omega$. When the sliding contact $C$ moves to point $E$, lamp $A$ lights up normally; when $C$ moves to point $F$, lamp $B$ lights up normally (points $E$ and $F$ are the endpoints of the rheostat). 1. What is the resistance of lamp $A$? 2. What is the internal resistance of the power supply? 3. What is the rated power of lamp $B$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bulb A on the left is connected in the main circuit, and is in series with the power supply and the right-side branch as a whole. The upper and lower two branches of the right-side part are connected between the same pair of terminals E and F: the lower branch is bulb B, and the upper branch is the sliding rheostat EF. The slider C is connected to the right end F through the upper wire, so the effective part of the rheostat connected to the two ends E and F is the EC segment; when C moves to E, EC=0, equivalent to E and F being short-circuited, and lamp B is bypassed; when C moves to F, EC is the entire rheostat EF, with resistance 180Ω, and is connected in parallel with lamp B. Reasoning calculation: Lamp A is marked “10V，10W”, so its resistance R_A=U_A^2/P_A=10^2/10=10Ω, and its normal luminous current I_A=P_A/U_A=10/10=1A. When C is at E, E and F are short-circuited; only lamp A and the power supply internal resistance r are in the main circuit, and A emits light normally, so the circuit current is 1A. The electromotive force of the power supply is 12V, and the voltage across lamp A is 10V, so the voltage across the internal resistance is 12-10=2V, hence r=2V/1A=2Ω. When C is at F, lamp B emits light normally, so the voltage across E and F is 9V; the voltage divided by the series part of lamp A and the power supply internal resistance is 12-9=3V, and their total resistance is R_A+r=10+2=12Ω, so the main-circuit current I=3/12=0.25A. At this time the current in the 180Ω rheostat branch is I_R=9/180=0.05A, therefore the current in lamp B is I_B=0.25-0.05=0.20A. The rated power of lamp B is P_B=U_B I_B=9×0.20=1.8W.
